recipes.name: admin-user-with-ssh-key
recipes.title: Admin user with SSH key
recipes.summary: A user account with no password, and the public keys that may log in as that user.

recipes.name: local-caching-resolver
recipes.title: Local caching resolver
recipes.summary: A DNS resolver for one client network, in its own jail: it caches, validates DNSSEC and answers only the clients you name.

recipes.name: local-dns-zone
recipes.title: Local DNS zone
recipes.summary: Names the resolver answers itself, for one zone: your own hosts, an internal domain, a name that points somewhere else inside.

recipes.name: nginx-tls-site
recipes.title: Nginx TLS site
recipes.summary: One https site on nginx with its certificate and key, and http redirecting to https; apply again with another name for the next site.

recipes.name: nginx-web-server
recipes.title: Nginx web server
recipes.summary: nginx installed and running, with a main configuration that includes conf.d/*.conf and answers nothing for a name no site claims.

recipes.name: postgresql-database-and-role
recipes.title: PostgreSQL database and role
recipes.summary: One database, the role that owns it, and the rule that lets that role connect from one network; apply again for the next database.

recipes.name: postgresql-nightly-backup
recipes.title: PostgreSQL nightly backup
recipes.summary: A nightly logical backup of every database and role of a PostgreSQL server, with retention; a failed night is never silent.

recipes.name: postgresql-restore-dump
recipes.title: Restore a PostgreSQL dump
recipes.summary: Restores one dump of the nightly backup into a new database, owned by the role you name.

recipes.name: quiet-periodic-and-cron
recipes.title: Quiet periodic and cron
recipes.summary: Periodic jobs that log instead of mailing, and cron jobs spread over a few seconds so that many jails do not wake together.

recipes.name: small-postgresql-server
recipes.title: Small PostgreSQL server
recipes.summary: A PostgreSQL server in a jail with its data in a volume, asking for a password on every network connection.

recipes.name: ssh-key-only-access
recipes.title: SSH key-only access
recipes.summary: sshd accepts key logins for the users you name and nothing else, after checking that every one of them has a key.

recipes.name: syslog-forwarding
recipes.title: Syslog forwarding
recipes.summary: The jail sends its log messages to a central log host over UDP, so they are kept somewhere other than the jail.
